name: IEWA World Women's Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own top women's title, defended in ten-woman and ten-man tag gauntlets as freely as in singles matches; Napualokelani carried it through a disqualification win over Jessica Starbird that ended with a run-in from GDWA's own World Champion. Created for an open cross-fed battle royal announced on 21 October 1997, to which SJPW, GDWA and the Modern-Day Wrestling Alliance all sent wrestlers.

name: IEWA Television Championship
epitaph: The fed's own weekly-broadcast title, defended twice in a row against former champion Richard Starr without a clean finish either time.

name: IEWA World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A title that changed hands between Japan Connection and Hysteria before the Disciples of Rage's own debut season, then drew a cage-match challenge on the strength of that history.

name: IEWA Women's Skyweight Championship
epitaph: A weight-class title for the fed's own lighter women's division, carried by Jun Shiratori into a locker-room-clearing brawl and swung as a weapon rather than defended on camera.

name: IEWA Women's Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: A title Jessica Starbird calls her first true win, distinguishing it from an earlier, amnesia-clouded match she does not fully remember for a since-vacated television title.

name: IEWA Women's Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A title held through the fed's own spring 1998 hiatus by the Prima Donnas, who spent the layoff at a Formula One race rather than in the ring.
